transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
I've just been feeling deeply depressed and sad for about two years now. It's been going on for so long, and I finally decided I needed to come in and get some help.
Have you experienced any periods of elevated mood or irritability, where you felt unusually happy, energetic, or restless, during these two years of feeling depressed?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. My mood has just been consistently low and depressed for the entire two years. I've never had periods of high energy or unusual happiness.

During these two years of feeling depressed, have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't, or had thoughts that seemed unreal or detached from reality?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and my thoughts have always stayed connected to reality.

Can you tell me more about your depressive symptoms over the past two years - have you had any periods where your symptoms improved or lifted for a while, or have they been consistently present the entire time?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether there were times when the feelings lifted. It just feels like it has been a constant weight for the last two years.
How have your depressive symptoms affected your daily life and relationships over the past two years, and have you been able to maintain your usual activities and responsibilities?

It has been extremely difficult to keep up with my normal activities and responsibilities over the last two years. I feel constantly exhausted physically and mentally, with absolutely no energy to do even basic daily chores. On top of that, my thinking feels so clouded and I struggle so much with concentration and indecisiveness that making simple daily choices has become completely overwhelming.

Given that your symptoms have lasted for two years, can you think of any two-month period during this time where you felt relatively symptom-free, or has it been a constant presence of depressive symptoms?

I'm not sure, but I really can't recall any clear two-month period where I felt completely free of these symptoms over the past two years. It feels like this heaviness has been a constant presence the entire time without any real break.
Is there anything else you'd like to share or discuss about your feelings or experiences over the past two years that might help me better understand your situation?

Over the last two years, I've felt this profound sense of emptiness and emotional numbness, as if all my feelings have just been completely dulled. My mind also constantly feels so foggy and clouded, which makes it incredibly hard to concentrate or make even simple daily decisions. It's just a very heavy and exhausting way to live.

Can you think of any specific period, even if brief, where your depressive symptoms were particularly severe, such as with significant changes in appetite, sleep, or feelings of worthlessness, which might have lasted for at least two weeks?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep or appetite, or had feelings of worthlessness. Instead, my low mood and fatigue have just been a constant, heavy presence for the last two years without those specific features.

Is there anything else you'd like to share or discuss about your feelings or experiences over the past two years that might help me better understand your situation, or do you feel like we've covered everything relevant to your care?

I think we have covered the main struggles. This combination of constant exhaustion, emotional numbness and emptiness, and foggy thinking has just been an incredibly heavy burden to carry continuously for the past two years.
It seems like we've discussed all the relevant aspects of your condition. I'm going to take some time to review our conversation and formulate a diagnosis and treatment plan tailored to your needs.

Thank you so much, Doctor, I really appreciate you taking the time to listen to me. I look forward to hearing your diagnosis and discussing the treatment plan you think would be best. Hopefully, we can find a way to help me start feeling better.
